questions.text: Which federal law in the United States primarily governs the privacy and security of patient health information?
questions.explanation: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act) establishes national standards for protecting patient health information.

questions.text: Which type of data is considered 'protected health information' (PHI) under HIPAA?

options.a: De-identified patient data shared for research
options.b: Aggregate statistical reports with no individual identifiers
options.c: Individually identifiable health information in any form

questions.explanation: PHI is any individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by a covered entity in any form — electronic, paper, or verbal.

questions.text: A hospital quality department is building a dashboard to monitor key performance indicators. Which principle BEST guides the selection of metrics?

options.a: Include as many metrics as possible to be comprehensive
options.b: Select metrics that are actionable, meaningful, and aligned with strategic goals
options.c: Use only metrics reported to external agencies

questions.explanation: Effective dashboards use a focused set of meaningful, actionable metrics aligned with organizational priorities rather than overwhelming stakeholders with data.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes 'data integrity' in healthcare information management?

options.a: The ability to access data from any location
options.b: The accuracy, completeness, and consistency of data
options.c: The speed at which data is processed
options.d: The volume of data stored in the system

questions.explanation: Data integrity refers to maintaining the accuracy, completeness, and consistency of data throughout its lifecycle.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of an electronic health record (EHR) in quality management?

options.a: To replace the need for clinical quality reviews
options.b: To support care coordination, documentation, and data-driven quality improvement
options.c: To reduce the number of clinical staff required

questions.explanation: EHRs support quality management by facilitating documentation, care coordination, and the extraction of data for quality measurement and improvement.

questions.text: Which statistical term describes the proportion of people with a condition who test positive for it?
questions.explanation: Sensitivity (true positive rate) measures how well a test identifies those who actually have the condition.

questions.text: A quality analyst is comparing infection rates across multiple hospital units. Which type of chart is MOST appropriate for this comparison?
questions.explanation: Bar charts are ideal for comparing discrete values across multiple categories or groups at a single point in time.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of 'secondary data' in healthcare quality?

options.c: Administrative claims data and medical records
options.d: Surveys completed by nursing staff during care

questions.explanation: Secondary data is collected for purposes other than the current study — administrative claims and existing medical records are classic examples.

questions.text: What does 'interoperability' mean in the context of health information technology?

options.a: The ability of different systems to exchange and use health information
options.b: The backup and recovery capabilities of an EHR system
options.c: The encryption standards used to protect data
options.d: The user interface design of a clinical system

questions.explanation: Interoperability allows different health IT systems to exchange, interpret, and use data effectively across organizations and settings.

questions.text: A hospital wants to reduce duplicate test ordering. Which information management tool would be MOST helpful?

options.b: Clinical decision support (CDS) integrated into the EHR

questions.explanation: Clinical decision support systems can alert providers to existing test results and flag duplicate orders in real time at the point of care.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes 'risk-adjusted' outcome data?

options.a: Data collected only from high-risk patient populations
options.b: Outcome data corrected for differences in patient demographics and severity of illness
options.d: Outcome data reported without any statistical adjustments

questions.explanation: Risk adjustment accounts for patient factors (age, comorbidities, severity) that affect outcomes, enabling fair comparisons across providers or facilities.

questions.text: Which data collection method involves systematically observing processes or behaviors as they occur?
questions.explanation: Direct observation captures real-time process performance, which is more accurate than self-reporting or retrospective data for measuring actual practice.

questions.text: In a data-driven quality culture, what is the PRIMARY role of data visualizations?

options.b: To make complex data accessible and actionable for decision-makers
options.c: To replace the need for narrative quality reports

questions.explanation: Effective data visualizations translate complex information into clear insights, enabling leaders and frontline staff to make informed decisions.

questions.text: A hospital is reviewing its data on central line-associated bloodstream infections (CLABSIs). The rate is 2.1 per 1,000 catheter days. This is an example of which type of measure?
questions.explanation: CLABSI rate per 1,000 catheter days is an outcome measure — it reflects the end result of care processes and patient safety practices.

questions.text: Which of the following is the MOST reliable method for measuring patient safety event rates?

options.b: Structured medical record review using trigger tools

questions.explanation: Trigger tools systematically review records for clues of adverse events, identifying far more events than voluntary reporting alone.
